plain_english: In a shrine or an outcaste hut, memory lost though, abandoning the body — freed simultaneous with knowing, going to isolation, sorrow killed.
sanskrit_cite: tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham | jñānasamakālamuktaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti hataśokaḥ

plain_english: Shrine-service for merit, outcaste-death for hell — but with no touch of merit-demerit stain, what use?
sanskrit_cite: puṇyāya tīrthasevā nirayāya śvapacasadananidhanagatiḥ | puṇyāpuṇyakalaṅkasparśābhāve tu kiṃ tena

plain_english: Throwing the well-separated rice-grain between husk-pieces makes not again that-form identity.
So the sheath-curtain-separated knowing, here by impression, standing though — freed self, untouched by that touch, becomes.
sanskrit_cite: tadvat kañcukapaṭalīpṛthakkṛtā saṃvid atra saṃskārāt | tiṣṭhanty api muktātmā tatsparśavivarjitā bhavati

plain_english: As flawless-made by the best artisan, the casket-bound gem, though stained, on cutting the bound shows clear truth.
sanskrit_cite: kuśalatamaśilpikalpitavimalībhāvaḥ samudgakopādheḥ | malino 'pi maṇir upādher vicchede svacchaparamārthaḥ

plain_english: So the true-teacher-taught pure state, feeling the body-bound, freed though void of other bounds, shines as Śiva-formed.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ sadguruśāsanavimalasthiti vedanaṃ tanūpādheḥ | muktam apy upādhyantaraśūnyam ivābhāti śivarūpam

plain_english: By scripture's weight, by unshaken faith become that — got before heaven, hell, man-ness.
sanskrit_cite: śāstrādiprāmāṇyād avicalitaśraddhayāpi tanmayatām | prāptaḥ sa eva pūrvaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ manuṣyatvam

plain_english: The last moment, nourishing a merit or demerit state, plays helper — but in going on, no cause.
sanskrit_cite: antyaḥ kṣaṇas tu tasmin puṇyāṃ pāpāṃ ca vā sthitiṃ puṣyan | mūḍhānāṃ sahakārībhāvaṃ gacchati gatau tu na sa hetuḥ

plain_english: Whoever knows that-self-ness — beast, bird, creeper and the rest — goes his own way, by old awakening impressed.
sanskrit_cite: ye 'pi tadātmatvena viduḥ paśupakṣisarīsṛpādayaḥ svagatim | te 'pi purātanasaṃbodhasaṃskṛtās tāṃ gatiṃ yānti
